entry.text: Eleven tents in a neat horseshoe on the moraine, guyed out, pegged down, rimed to a finish like sugar work. Inside the big mess tent, six climbers are sitting round a stove that went out sixty years ago, and they are not dead. Their eyes track you. Nothing else moves, because nothing else can at minus forty in a body that has been paused since the first winter, but the eyes track you, and every single one of them is furious, and all six pairs are pointed at the same man, and the man is holding the kettle.

choices.label: Strip the store tents and leave the mess tent shut
Light the stove. It is the decent thing to do.

the_stores.text: An expedition provisioned for three months above four thousand metres, abandoned at week two: crates of high-altitude rations, fuel bottles by the dozen, oxygen, a doctor's kit that would set you up for a year, rope, hardware, and a summit cache nobody ever went up to collect. In the mess tent, pinned to the centre pole at eye height, is the rota. Every column is ticked. Every column except one. Sixty years ago it was Bewley's turn to make the tea and Bewley had a headache and said he would do it in a minute.

choices.label: Make the tea yourself and end it
Take the kettle out of Bewley's hands

bewley.text: You brew up. Six mugs. You put them down one by one and the tent fills with steam for the first time in six decades, and the ice on their eyelashes goes, and the argument that has been running silently in that tent since before your grandparents finally, finally ends. Bewley says sorry. Everyone says it's fine. Nobody means it and everybody accepts it, which is how these things conclude. Then they tell you where the summit cache is, and the route up to it, and which crevasse to avoid, and where Hollis kept the expedition funds — and then, in their own time, in the warm, in the order they sat down in, they stop. The tent is very quiet. There is still tea in the pot.

the_guy_line.text: A guy line at minus forty is a wire, not a rope. You catch one at shin height in the dark between tents and it does not give at all, and neither, it turns out, does your shin.

the_thaw.text: You light the stove and the nearest climber thaws faster than the rest, which is not a mercy, because sixty years of frozen tissue does not come back in the order it went. She gets one hand working. She uses it on you, and she is not aiming, she is just finally able to move.

wrong_brew.text: You make it wrong. You make it with the boiled snow rather than the good water, which was Hollis's rule, and Hollis has been sitting in that chair for sixty years with an opinion about it. Six pairs of eyes move at once. You have never been looked at like that and you would rather have been hit.

the_argument.text: You take the kettle. That is a side. The moment you take a side, sixty years of held-in grievance finds a channel, and six people who cannot move discover that they can move a little after all, and the mess tent becomes a very small room containing a very old argument and you.
